unit.why: A short piece of advice to a man who admits he is quick-tempered (do not grate onions, since grating is bad for an angry hasid), followed by a fragmentary saying of R. Naftali of Ropshitz about a long onion. The visitor only frames the saying, so there is no real narrative event.
unit.boundary_note: The Ropshitz saying is cut off at the end of the division ('ברענגט סך'). The speaker of the first saying is referred to only as 'לפניו', so his identity depends on the previous division. The next division begins with new sayings of the Lublin rebbe.
